{
  "technical_and_design_decisions": [
    "Implement the increment within the existing Spring-based Java project and preserve its current public APIs unless a requirement explicitly requires a compatible extension.",
    "Expose timeout and pollInterval as optional global DSL-level properties, with existing defaults retained when the properties are not specified.",
    "Use the project's existing configuration model and builder/parser conventions for DSL and XML generation rather than introducing a parallel configuration mechanism.",
    "Upgrade Spring Integration to version 4.2.1 using the project's existing dependency-management and build conventions, resolving source and test compatibility issues as needed.",
    "Refactor JobLaunchingTasklet conservatively to improve performance without changing externally observable job-launching semantics.",
    "Implement inline SpEL support at stream-definition scope by resolving expressions through the existing Spring expression infrastructure and applying the same behavior to built-in and custom modules.",
    "Represent YARN undeployed as an explicit status in the existing YARN SPI status model and map it consistently from the relevant YARN lifecycle state.",
    "Split the admin artifact and Hadoop-distribution-specific dependencies into separate build artifacts or dependency profiles while retaining a usable default build.",
    "Extend automated tests at unit, DSL parsing, XML generation, integration, and regression levels using the project's existing test framework.",
    "Publish job orchestration guidance in the existing project documentation format and link it from the relevant documentation index."
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "The increment is implemented by one developer familiar with Java, Spring, Spring Integration, the project DSL, XML configuration, Maven or Gradle, and YARN-related code.",
    "The repository, build, and existing test suite are available and buildable at the start of the work.",
    "The specification does not require new user-interface work, database schema changes, migration tooling, or changes to public protocols beyond the named features.",
    "Spring Integration 4.2.1 is compatible with the project's required Java and Spring versions, or compatibility adjustments are limited to normal source and configuration changes.",
    "Existing defaults for timeout and pollInterval can be identified from the current implementation and remain backward compatible.",
    "The JobLaunchingTasklet refactor is limited to the current module and does not require redesigning the broader batch execution architecture.",
    "The existing SpEL infrastructure can be reused; no new expression language, sandbox, or security model is required.",
    "YARN provides or exposes enough lifecycle information to distinguish undeployed from unknown without requiring changes to external YARN services.",
    "The admin artifact split can be achieved through build and dependency restructuring without maintaining every possible Hadoop distribution as a separately developed codebase.",
    "Documentation requires technical guidance and examples but no localization, formal UX review, or external publishing process.",
    "Effort includes implementation, developer-level testing, code review preparation, documentation updates, and local regression verification, but excludes elapsed waiting time and release-management work performed by other teams."
  ],
  "activities": [
    {
      "activity_id": "A1",
      "activity_name": "Repository analysis and implementation planning",
      "activity_description": "Inspect the existing DSL, XML generation, Spring Integration integration, JobLaunchingTasklet, YARN SPI, admin packaging, build configuration, and test structure; identify affected classes and establish the implementation sequence.",
      "most_likely_effort": 3
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A2",
      "activity_name": "Implement global DSL timeout and pollInterval options",
      "activity_description": "Add optional timeout and pollInterval properties at the Flo DSL level, propagate them to the appropriate runtime components, preserve existing defaults, and add focused validation and unit tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 5
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A3",
      "activity_name": "Upgrade Spring Integration to 4.2.1",
      "activity_description": "Update dependency and build declarations, resolve API or behavior changes, adapt affected production code and tests, and verify that the project compiles and starts with the upgraded dependency.",
      "most_likely_effort": 8
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A4",
      "activity_name": "Review and refactor JobLaunchingTasklet",
      "activity_description": "Profile or inspect the current tasklet execution path, remove avoidable overhead, simplify resource and state handling, preserve existing behavior, and add regression coverage for successful and failing job launches.",
      "most_likely_effort": 8
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A5",
      "activity_name": "Add DSL and XML generation variant coverage",
      "activity_description": "Expand automated tests for combinations of global options, stream definitions, module types, XML output variants, defaults, omissions, and invalid configurations.",
      "most_likely_effort": 7
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A6",
      "activity_name": "Implement inline SpEL expressions at stream definition level",
      "activity_description": "Extend stream parsing and runtime configuration so inline SpEL expressions can operate on payloads consistently for out-of-the-box and custom modules, including expression evaluation, error handling, and representative tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 10
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A7",
      "activity_name": "Write job orchestration documentation",
      "activity_description": "Create user-oriented documentation describing job orchestration concepts, recommended workflow construction, relevant configuration, examples, and links to related DSL or batch documentation.",
      "most_likely_effort": 3
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A8",
      "activity_name": "Add undeployed status to the YARN SPI",
      "activity_description": "Extend the status enumeration or model, update YARN state mapping and serialization or presentation paths, and add tests proving undeployed is distinguished from unknown.",
      "most_likely_effort": 4
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A9",
      "activity_name": "Split the admin artifact from Hadoop-distribution-specific libraries",
      "activity_description": "Restructure modules, artifacts, dependency scopes, and build profiles so the admin artifact does not pull all Hadoop distribution variants, while preserving supported packaging and adding dependency-resolution tests or verification.",
      "most_likely_effort": 8
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A10",
      "activity_name": "Cross-feature integration and regression testing",
      "activity_description": "Run the complete build and test suite, exercise representative end-to-end DSL, XML, Spring Integration, YARN, and packaging scenarios, diagnose regressions, and apply corrective fixes.",
      "most_likely_effort": 6
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A11",
      "activity_name": "Final code quality and delivery preparation",
      "activity_description": "Perform final cleanup, API and compatibility review, update release notes or change documentation where customary, verify reproducible packaging, and prepare the increment for submission.",
      "most_likely_effort": 3
    }
  ],
  "reported_total": {
    "most_likely_effort": 65
  }
}

technical_and_design_decisions: Implement the increment within the existing Spring-based Java project and preserve its current public APIs unless a requirement explicitly requires a compatible extension.
Expose timeout and pollInterval as optional global DSL-level properties, with existing defaults retained when the properties are not specified.
Use the project's existing configuration model and builder/parser conventions for DSL and XML generation rather than introducing a parallel configuration mechanism.
Upgrade Spring Integration to version 4.2.1 using the project's existing dependency-management and build conventions, resolving source and test compatibility issues as needed.
Refactor JobLaunchingTasklet conservatively to improve performance without changing externally observable job-launching semantics.
Implement inline SpEL support at stream-definition scope by resolving expressions through the existing Spring expression infrastructure and applying the same behavior to built-in and custom modules.
Represent YARN undeployed as an explicit status in the existing YARN SPI status model and map it consistently from the relevant YARN lifecycle state.
Split the admin artifact and Hadoop-distribution-specific dependencies into separate build artifacts or dependency profiles while retaining a usable default build.
Extend automated tests at unit, DSL parsing, XML generation, integration, and regression levels using the project's existing test framework.
Publish job orchestration guidance in the existing project documentation format and link it from the relevant documentation index.
assumptions: The increment is implemented by one developer familiar with Java, Spring, Spring Integration, the project DSL, XML configuration, Maven or Gradle, and YARN-related code.
The repository, build, and existing test suite are available and buildable at the start of the work.
The specification does not require new user-interface work, database schema changes, migration tooling, or changes to public protocols beyond the named features.
Spring Integration 4.2.1 is compatible with the project's required Java and Spring versions, or compatibility adjustments are limited to normal source and configuration changes.
Existing defaults for timeout and pollInterval can be identified from the current implementation and remain backward compatible.
The JobLaunchingTasklet refactor is limited to the current module and does not require redesigning the broader batch execution architecture.
The existing SpEL infrastructure can be reused; no new expression language, sandbox, or security model is required.
YARN provides or exposes enough lifecycle information to distinguish undeployed from unknown without requiring changes to external YARN services.
The admin artifact split can be achieved through build and dependency restructuring without maintaining every possible Hadoop distribution as a separately developed codebase.
Documentation requires technical guidance and examples but no localization, formal UX review, or external publishing process.

Effort includes implementation, developer-level testing, code review preparation, documentation updates, and local regression verification, but excludes elapsed waiting time and release-management work performed by other teams.
